content:
I very much enjoyed teaching a math/cs course on cryptography in Fall 22. |

The programming component was in Go because that was a different time for Lean 4. I need to start thinking about teaching for Fall '24 and it is clear that Lean is mature enough to handle everything in that course. But a greater focus on post-quantum algorithms might better survive the test of time.

I haven't thought deeply about how to structure the course. If people have thoughts, please share.

I am 3 years late on this discussion, but I hope you're still interested in the topic. I'm a PhD candidate in post-quantum cryptography and have been a TA twice in Clemson's Intro to crypto class. I'm also getting an Engineering and Science Education graduate certificate, so I have read the math ed research literature extensively. When I started experimenting with Lean, I thought it might be a good idea to use Lean to teach crypto, similarly to how Ed Dubinsky used ISETL to teach algebra.
